response.sql: WITH orders_in_range AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, c.gender FROM Orders o INNER JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.date_order_placed > '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND o.date_order_placed < '2017-05-24 19:26:44'), gender_counts AS (SELECT gender, COUNT(*) as order_count FROM orders_in_range GROUP BY gender), average_count AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) as avg_count FROM gender_counts) SELECT gc.gender, gc.order_count, gc.order_count - ac.avg_count as above_average FROM gender_counts gc CROSS JOIN average_count ac WHERE gc.order_count > ac.avg_count ORDER BY gc.gender

assumptions.assumption: Text comparison directive: The request specifies 'comparing date_order_placed as text', but the column is DATETIME. The primary query uses standard datetime comparison with > and <, which databases handle natively for DATETIME values compared to ISO 8601 timestamp strings. This produces correct chronological ordering.

alternatives.interpretation: If literal text/lexicographic comparison is required despite the DATETIME column type, explicitly cast the column to character before comparison.
alternatives.sql: WITH orders_in_range AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, c.gender FROM Orders o INNER JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE CAST(o.date_order_placed AS CHAR) > '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS CHAR) < '2017-05-24 19:26:44'), gender_counts AS (SELECT gender, COUNT(*) as order_count FROM orders_in_range GROUP BY gender), average_count AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) as avg_count FROM gender_counts) SELECT gc.gender, gc.order_count, gc.order_count - ac.avg_count as above_average FROM gender_counts gc CROSS JOIN average_count ac WHERE gc.order_count > ac.avg_count ORDER BY gc.gender
